title: Format an expense line
prompt: An expense arrived from a form with messy text. Build the string `line` so that it reads exactly `Coffee with Sam: $4.50 (food)`, then log it. Use the variables: trim `rawLabel` and capitalise its first letter, show `cents` as dollars with two decimals, and lowercase `category`. A template literal keeps this readable.
hints: Start with `const trimmed = rawLabel.trim();` so the first character is the letter c, not a space.
`trimmed[0].toUpperCase() + trimmed.slice(1)` capitalises the first letter. `(cents / 100).toFixed(2)` gives `"4.50"`.
explanation: Each string method returns a new string, so the solution stores each step under its own name: `trimmed`, then `label`. Doing the trim first matters, because in the raw text index 0 is a space. `toFixed(2)` turns `4.5` into the text `"4.50"`, which is what people expect to see for money. The template literal then reads almost like the output itself; the first `$` in `$${price}` is a literal dollar sign and the second starts the insertion.

checks.trimmed: Starts with a capital C and has no stray spaces
